scientificQuestion: For each of C-FF and IDFF, does the frozen managed fixed-worker-pool implementation provide statistically supported and practically important reductions in matched batch wall time as physical-core worker count increases within one CCD, while dual-CCD W16-versus-W8 scaling is retained as a gated key-secondary characterization and all correctness and oracle hard gates remain satisfied?
paperRole: supplemental managed multi-query deployment and scalability evidence that strengthens the existing paper; not a second main algorithm-ranking experiment

endpoint.singleCcdEstimand: within-block equal-weight OLS slope of log(batchWallSeconds) on log2(workerCount) for W1 W2 W4 W8

mipe.primaryInterpretation: at least 10 percent lower batch wall time per worker doubling
mipe.secondaryInterpretation: at least 10 percent lower batch wall time for W16 versus W8
mipe.role: planning alternative and practical-importance threshold; superiority null remains zero

primary.multiplicity: Holm strong FWER across exactly P1-P4
primary.claimRule: Holm-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05, multiplicity-compatible confidence interval below zero, and point estimate at or beyond the MIPE

keySecondary.gate: open only if all four primary hypotheses are rejected by their frozen Holm procedure
keySecondary.claimRule: when the gate opens, Holm-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05, multiplicity-compatible confidence interval below zero, and point estimate at or beyond the MIPE; otherwise estimates and intervals are descriptive only

power.selectionRule: smallest B whose worst of four Holm-adjusted opaque-primary Monte Carlo rejection-power Wilson 95 percent lower bounds is at least 0.90
power.noPassingCandidate: stop without final implementation or schedule freeze and request a separately authorized redesign

correctnessAndStopping.failurePolicy: fail closed and preserve the entire failed attempt; any successor requires wholly new execution measured delivery and acceptance roots
